reference.rule: Every implementation task must name its Hermes source symbol or document an intentional Canvas divergence.

executionPolicy.commitPolicy: one focused commit per completed package
executionPolicy.impactPolicy: Run GitNexus upstream impact before editing every symbol and warn on HIGH or CRITICAL risk.
executionPolicy.changePolicy: Run GitNexus detect_changes against main before every commit.
executionPolicy.browserPolicy: Playwright or Chrome testing requires explicit user approval and must use localhost:3000.
executionPolicy.containerPolicy: Do not build or start containers unless explicitly requested.

gates.evidence: Hermes commit and MIT license are pinned, compliance artifacts pass, PR #106 is merged, and parity fixtures exist.
Threshold, effective-input-budget, cheap-gate and greater-than-five-percent progress tests match Hermes semantics.
Active user and assistant anchors survive, tool groups are atomic, and every cut is token-budgeted.
Pruning is idempotent, savings-gated, media-safe and skill-aware.
Exact non-sensitive anchors, verbatim user messages, chunk digests and authorized session_search recovery pass.
Rolling summary, focus, feasibility, redaction and fail-closed behavior pass multi-cycle tests.
SQLite and PostgreSQL pass lock, watermark, stale, timeout, anti-thrash and late-worker tests.
Live, automation, manual, idle, pre-send and overflow paths use one engine and never knowingly send an oversized request.
Provider actual, next estimate, effective budget, trigger and target are distinct and UI-tested after approval.
Shadow rollout, default decision, rollback, compliance, tests, lint, build and approved E2E are complete.
